history.label: Pertinent Medical History
history.hint: Diagnoses, hospitalizations, surgeries, and comorbidities that impact function.

plof.label: Prior Level of Function
plof.hint: Independence level, mobility, ADLs, and baseline function before this episode.

clof.label: Current Level of Function
clof.hint: Current deficits, assistance required, mobility limitations, and safety concerns. Include device use and task limits.

objective.label: Objective Findings
objective.hint: Strength deficits with functional relevance, ROM limitations, balance deficits, gait deviations, transfer ability, pain and its functional impact.

assessment.label: Assessment
assessment.hint: Key impairments, functional impact, rehab potential, and need for skilled therapy.

necessity.label: Skilled Need / Medical Necessity
necessity.hint: Why skilled therapy is required, why the patient cannot safely progress independently, and the risk without therapy: falls, decline, hospitalization.

homebound.label: Homebound Status
homebound.hint: Functional limitations restricting leaving home, assistance required (device, caregiver, effort, pain), and why leaving home requires considerable and taxing effort. Concrete reasons, never generic wording alone.

goals.label: Goals
goals.hint: Functional, measurable, realistic, time-bound. One statement per goal.

poc.label: Plan of Care
poc.hint: Frequency and duration, treatment focus, and progression strategy.

exlog.label: Exercise Log
exlog.hint: Exercises performed, muscle groups targeted, techniques and devices used, and purpose related to function.

progress.label: Progress Summary
progress.hint: Prior status versus current, with improvements, plateaus, or decline stated plainly and backed by measures.

education.label: Patient/Caregiver Education & Injury Prevention
education.hint: What was taught, to whom, and whether reinforcement is needed for carryover.

interventions.label: Skilled Interventions Provided
interventions.hint: Labeled paragraphs, each on its own line, covering the interventions actually performed.

caregiving.label: Caregiving
caregiving.hint: Who assists, with what, and at what support level. Name the specific tasks the aide or caregiver performs.

meds.label: Medication Management
meds.hint: Independent or requires assistance. Only known issues, recent changes, compliance concerns, or education provided. No unsupported medication detail.

social.label: Social History
social.hint: Who they live with, home setup, and available support.

precautions.label: Precautions and Restrictions
precautions.hint: Weight bearing status and any imposed restrictions: no lifting, carrying, bending, twisting.

referral.label: Reason for Referral
referral.hint: Primary reason for referral and any other reasons an evaluation is required.

functional.label: Functional Assessment
functional.hint: Structured narrative, each component its own paragraph: therapy education provided (safety, pain management, HEP, ADLs, fall prevention, caregiver training, equipment use); medication status including changes or confirmation of none; functional limitations across mobility, strength, balance, endurance, posture, transfers, gait, safety awareness, ADLs; skilled interventions performed; patient or caregiver response including understanding, participation, tolerance.

noa.label: NOA Communication — SOC
noa.hint: Complete SOC narrative using each of these as its own paragraph heading, in order: patient discharged from; primary reason for referral; pertinent medical history; scheduled physician follow up; prior level of function; current level of function including mobility, transfers, ADLs, fall risk; caregiving support; medication management status; skilled care needs including clinical reasoning and need for a licensed therapist; response to initial interventions; homebound status; medical necessity; addendum with environmental or safety concerns; communication with physician or agent including approval of plan of care; disciplines ordered.

summary.label: Recertification Summary
summary.hint: Disciplines being recertified, ongoing functional limitations, certifying practitioner, and review of the plan of care for the next 60 day certification period.

necessity2.label: Medical Necessity
necessity2.hint: Why continued skilled services are necessary to improve safety and independence, reduce fall risk, and prevent decline, injury, or hospitalization. If HHA is ordered, document the personal care needs still requiring aide support.

addendum.label: Addendum
addendum.hint: Physician oversight, plan of care review, recertification discussed with the practitioner or authorized representative, date and time, and approval for the next certification period.

disciplines.label: Disciplines Ordered
disciplines.hint: PT, SN, OT, ST, HHA as applicable.

change.label: Change in Condition
change.hint: How symptoms or condition are changing. Compare the patient before the condition started to now. No vital signs.

subjective.label: Subjective
subjective.hint: Anything the patient says describing their symptoms. Numerals as numbers.

patientgoals.label: Patient's Stated Goals
patientgoals.hint: What the patient said their goals are, in their terms.

impaired.label: Impaired Functional Activities
impaired.hint: Ten or more functional activities specifically mentioned as impaired or expected to be impaired given the condition. Lower extremity conditions imply walking, stairs, bed mobility, floor to stand, carrying between rooms. Upper extremity conditions imply lifting, pushing, pulling, carrying, side lying sleep, overhead reach, dressing, bathing, grooming.

stg.label: Short Term Goals (6 weeks)
stg.hint: SMART goals written to Medicare guidelines in narrative format. One goal each for bed mobility, transfers, gait, strengthening, balance, pain, ROM, lung capacity, standardized test, RTM, telehealth, caregiver and patient education for mobility safety and HEP, and wheelchair.

ltg.label: Long Term Goals (12 weeks)
ltg.hint: Same goal categories as short term, written to the 12 week horizon.

effectiveness.label: Effectiveness of Current Plan of Care
effectiveness.hint: Personalize with the dictated measures where available.

variables.label: Variable Factors Influencing Response
variables.hint: Keep the approved wording; adjust to the factors actually present.

outcomes.label: Outcome Measures Utilized
outcomes.hint: Keep only the measures actually used this visit.

justification.label: Justification for Continued Skilled Services
justification.hint: Personalize the deficits to this patient.

response.label: Patient/Caregiver Response
response.hint: Tolerance of treatment, cues or assistance required, understanding demonstrated, and carryover.

Do not include the section prompts or instructions in the output.

Effectiveness of Current Plan of Care
sections.hint: Personalize with the dictated measures where available.
sections.boiler: The current plan of care is effective as evidenced by measurable improvements in range of motion, strength, and functional mobility. Patient demonstrates increased ambulation tolerance, improved transfer ability, and progression toward use of a less restrictive assistive device. Pain has overall decreased and is responsive to skilled interventions. Objective measures and functional performance indicate appropriate progression, supporting continuation of the current treatment approach.

sections.label: Variable Factors Influencing Response
sections.hint: Keep the approved wording; adjust to the factors actually present.
sections.boiler: Patient response to treatment is influenced by variable factors including pain fluctuations with activity, soft tissue restrictions, postural impairments, and underlying weakness and deconditioning. Additional contributing factors include reduced endurance, fatigue with activity, and neuromuscular impairments affecting gait and balance. These variables require ongoing skilled assessment and modification of interventions to ensure safe and effective progression.

sections.label: Impact of Co-Morbidities
sections.hint: Name the comorbidities actually reported.
sections.boiler: Patient's co-morbid conditions, including neuromuscular deficits, deconditioning, and cardiopulmonary limitations, contribute to impaired strength, endurance, balance, and functional mobility. These conditions slow recovery, increase fall risk, and necessitate continued skilled monitoring and intervention to safely progress rehabilitation.

sections.label: Objective Evidence Supporting Continued Progress
sections.hint: Insert the dictated measures.
sections.boiler: Patient demonstrates objective improvements in ROM, strength, and functional mobility, supported by measurable changes in standardized outcome tools and clinical assessment. Despite ongoing deficits, patient shows clear capacity for continued improvement with skilled intervention based on current trajectory and response to treatment.

sections.label: Outcome Measures Utilized
sections.hint: Keep only the measures actually used this visit.
sections.boiler: Objective outcome measures include Timed Up and Go (TUG), 2-Minute Walk Test, goniometric ROM measurements, manual muscle testing (MMT), gait and postural assessment, and Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS). These tools are used to quantify progress, guide clinical decision-making, and support medical necessity.

sections.label: Justification for Continued Skilled Services
sections.hint: Personalize the deficits to this patient.
sections.boiler: Patient continues to require skilled physical therapy due to persistent deficits in strength, balance, gait mechanics, endurance, and functional mobility. Skilled intervention is necessary for clinical decision-making, manual therapy, gait retraining, and progression of therapeutic exercise. A home exercise program alone is insufficient due to complexity of impairments and need for skilled cueing and monitoring. Without continued therapy, patient is at risk for functional decline, increased fall risk, and delayed recovery.

rules: Paragraph format unless otherwise specified.
Never use the patient's name.
Do not include the section prompts in the output.
Do not use hyphens.
Do not invent information.

sections.label: Goals
sections.hint: Functional, measurable, time-framed, addressing mobility, transfers, gait, strength, balance, endurance, or ROM. Add condition specific goals where applicable: diabetes gets foot care and education, fall risk gets a fall prevention goal, pain gets a functional pain management goal. One statement per goal.

sections.label: Homebound Statement

sections.label: Medical Necessity

profiles.name: Medicare Recertification Narrative
rules: Paragraph format. Never use the patient's name.
State the qualifying skilled service, why the patient remains homebound in concrete functional terms, and why skilled care is still needed now.
Include measurable progress and the deficits that remain.
Confirm physician or allowed practitioner oversight and plan of care review.
Do not document case mix scoring, payer gaming language, or unverified utilization history.
Do not add unsupported medication details.

sections.label: Recertification Summary
sections.hint: Disciplines being recertified, ongoing functional limitations, certifying practitioner, and review of the plan of care for the next 60 day certification period.

sections.label: Current Level of Function
sections.hint: Continued limitations in mobility, ADLs, transfers, gait, balance, endurance, posture, with level of assistance for specific tasks. Include device use and task limits, e.g. limited household distances with walker, wheelchair otherwise, assist for shower transfers.

sections.label: Caregiving
sections.hint: Who assists, with what, and at what support level (intermittent, daily, full time, limited). Name the specific tasks the aide or caregiver performs.

sections.label: Skilled Care Need
sections.hint: Deficits driving continued skilled service, and why reassessment, progression, safety monitoring, caregiver education, and plan of care updates cannot be performed by unskilled personnel.

sections.label: Response to Interventions
sections.hint: Progress, partial progress, or limited progress with subjective and objective evidence. Use measurable examples. State clearly that progress is incomplete and deficits remain.

sections.label: Medical Necessity
sections.hint: Why continued skilled services are necessary to improve safety and independence, reduce fall risk, and prevent decline, injury, or hospitalization. If HHA is ordered, document the personal care needs still requiring aide support.

sections.label: Addendum
sections.hint: Physician oversight, plan of care review, recertification discussed with the practitioner or authorized representative, date and time, and approval for the next certification period.

sections.hint: PT, SN, OT, ST, HHA as applicable.

snippets.label: Interventions Provided to Prevent Further Injury
snippets.text: Skilled education/intervention provided to reduce risk of further injury, falls, and post-surgical complications. Patient/caregiver instructed in precautions, safe mobility strategies, pacing, environmental awareness, and activity modification. Reinforcement needed for safety and carryover.

snippets.label: Assistive Device Instruction for Home Safety
snippets.text: Patient instructed in basic use of assistive device for safe household mobility, including keeping device close, turning slowly, avoiding excessive reaching, maintaining clear pathways, and using caregiver supervision as needed. AD safety reviewed due to fall risk and home setup. Reinforcement needed.

snippets.label: Environmental / Safety Issues to Be Resolved
snippets.text: Home safety concerns include [tight spaces / clutter / throw rugs / poor lighting / pet-related trip hazards / tubing management / stairs or ramp safety / bathroom access / other]. Patient/caregiver instructed to maintain clear pathways, improve lighting, remove hazards, secure tubing/cords, and use supervision as needed. Reinforcement needed.

snippets.label: Fall Risk / Balance Skilled Intervention
snippets.text: Skilled intervention provided to address balance deficits and elevated fall risk. Patient instructed in safe turning, controlled transfers, pacing, upright posture, visual focus during mobility, and stopping/resting if unsteady or dizzy. Skilled PT required for ongoing balance progression and fall prevention training.

snippets.label: HEP Instruction Provided
snippets.text: HEP instruction provided to improve strength, balance, mobility, and carryover between visits. Patient instructed in [LE exercises / seated exercises / standing balance / walking program / transfer practice / vestibular or visual tracking exercises / breathing or pacing strategies] within tolerance and precautions. Patient/caregiver instructed to stop with increased pain, dizziness, shortness of breath, or unsafe symptoms. Reinforcement needed.

snippets.label: Transfers / Gait Skilled Intervention
snippets.text: Skilled intervention provided to address deficits in transfers and gait impacting household mobility and safety. Patient instructed in controlled sit-to-stand sequencing, slow positional changes, safe turning, posture, pacing, AD use as applicable, and caregiver supervision as needed. Gait training focused on safest mobility strategy in the home while reducing fall risk and maintaining precautions.
